1	# Repository and module layout
2	
3	Recorded 2026-09-10 from the user's agreement on repository organization, CLI
4	naming and the browser report. This chapter is the single current home for
5	those structural decisions and the remaining crate/package design. Its companion
6	file inventory owns the proposed target filenames and generates the tables below. It records
7	user-agreed direction; technical integration and independent review remain
8	pending. It grants no implementation readiness or authorization. The
9	[central register](08-decision-and-readiness-register.md#unified-product-design-readiness)
10	continues to own readiness.
11	
12	The [implementation boundaries and build plan](implementation-boundaries-and-build-plan.md)
13	owns the concrete API handoff, private recovery record/failure matrix,
14	generation/build rules, tooling decision matrix and source-bound milestone coverage.
15	The [prototype report inventory](prototype-report-inventory.md) owns its 24
16	feature dispositions. These focused companions extend this layout without
17	creating alternate readiness records; both are author proposals pending Claude.
18	
19	## Agreed organization
20	
21	Settle the major package boundaries before implementation. Each package needs a
22	clear responsibility, public interface, permitted dependencies and build output.
23	Individual source files and small internal module divisions can evolve within
24	those boundaries during implementation.
25	
26	The proposed product source tree is:
27	
28	```text
29	apps/
30	  cli/                  Command-line application and host assembly
31	  report/               Browser report interface, styles and assets
32	crates/
33	  reporting/            Host-owned report projection and HTML assembly
34	  contracts/            Shared inert contract types (proposed)
35	  identity/             Pure canonical admission and identities (proposed)
36	  evaluator/            Pure evaluation and semantic replay (proposed)
37	  platform/             OS mechanisms (proposed)
38	  security/             Trust, custody and grants (proposed)
39	  storage/              Retained evidence mechanics (proposed)
40	  components/           Component supervision and protocols (proposed)
41	  lifecycle/            Install/update/recovery coordination (proposed)
42	  host/                 Host authority and workflows (proposed)
43	providers/
44	  typescript/           TypeScript/JavaScript provider
45	  rust/                 Rust provider and its toolchain boundary
46	schemas/                Owned wire contracts and binding generation
47	tests/
48	  conformance/          Shared contract and compatibility checks
49	  integration/          Complete workflows across component boundaries
50	  qualification/        Platform and performance evidence requirements
51	tools/                  Build, release and repository maintenance
52	docs/                   Current product and developer documentation
53	```
54	
55	This is the target organization for implementation. These directories have not
56	been scaffolded by this decision. It does not move the existing architecture
57	record or its pinned schema and evidence files. The initial inventory below
58	proposes crate boundaries and direct dependencies for review. Complete API,
59	workspace and build configuration decisions remain open.
60	
61	### CLI names
62	
63	Directory, Cargo package and installed executable have distinct purposes:
64	
65	| Item | Agreed name |
66	|---|---|
67	| Source directory | `apps/cli/` |
68	| Cargo package | `opensip-cli` |
69	| Installed executable | `opensip` |
70	
71	The CLI assembles and invokes host services. Its directory name does not move
72	semantic authority into argument parsing or presentation code.
73	
74	### Report ownership and delivery
75	
76	The browser report has its own source home at `apps/report/`. Report-specific
77	components, styles and browser assets stay together there. A generic
78	`packages/ui/` is reserved for a future demonstrated need to share visual
79	components between applications; it is not part of the initial package list.
80	
81	`crates/reporting/` owns preparation of host-approved report data and assembly
82	of the HTML output with its built assets. The inventory now proposes the Cargo
83	package name `opensip-reporting` and one renderer module per applicable output
84	format in that crate. Those refinements require technical review; only the
85	directory and report responsibility were agreed in the initial discussion.
86	
87	The responsibilities follow the existing
88	[workflow output contract](../contracts/product-v1/workflows-and-surfaces.md#8-command-inventory-outputs-and-parity-ar-13-surfaces-ar-16):
89	
90	1. The admitted analysis and host evaluation produce findings, evidence and
91	   assessments under their existing authority rules.
92	2. The host prepares the declared report projection. Reporting code preserves
93	   those values and assembles the deliverable.
94	3. The browser interface presents the embedded data. Any agreed filtering or
95	   navigation changes presentation, without recomputing policy or changing the
96	   underlying findings, evidence, verdict or completeness disclosures.
97	
98	The selected HTML deliverable remains a self-contained, offline file with its
99	data embedded and no script-fetched data. It requires no separately running
100	web server. Building `apps/report/` produces assets for that deliverable;
101	placing its source under `apps/` does not select a hosted service, server-side
102	rendering or a separate installation. Exact build, asset inclusion and release
103	packaging mechanisms remain to be specified under the common signed closure
104	and offline delivery contracts. No frontend framework or bundler is selected
105	by this directory decision.
106	
107	The prototype's source has now been inventoried at its pinned commit in the
108	[report inventory](prototype-report-inventory.md), with 24 proposed preservation,
109	change or deferral dispositions and reasons. HTML output is selected; executed
110	feature parity and independent acceptance have not yet been established. Any
111	change to the current offline or data-access contract needs explicit review.
112	
113	## Rules for a maintainable repository
114	
115	- Give every contract and shared type one source owner. Generate language
116	  bindings or enforce explicit drift checks; do not maintain competing copies
117	  by hand.
118	- Document the allowed dependency direction and enforce it in repository
119	  checks. Preserve the pure evaluator's lack of effects and the host's
120	  authority over admission, lifecycle, persistence and outcomes.
121	- Create a crate when it establishes a useful dependency boundary, isolates
122	  substantial dependencies, or supports independent testing or delivery.
123	  Smaller responsibilities may remain internal modules. A directory does not
124	  imply a process, separately installed component or independent release.
125	- Define provider workspaces and toolchain requirements explicitly so unrelated
126	  provider dependencies do not become mandatory CLI build dependencies.
127	  Independent releases continue to use the common compatibility and packaging
128	  contracts; directory layout does not introduce lockstep versions.
129	- Keep unit tests near their implementation. Give shared fixtures,
130	  conformance checks, integration tests and qualification workloads explicit
131	  homes and owners. Reference fixtures do not become product qualification
132	  merely by being copied into a test directory.
133	- Maintain one current documentation reading path. Update the owning document
134	  as decisions evolve and use version control for its history. Keep retained
135	  audit/review evidence clearly identified and linked without duplicating the
136	  current design across successive status documents.
137	- Keep build outputs and temporary agent work out of the normal source tree.
138	  Generated bindings have the explicit locations below; the build plan proposes
139	  checking them in with byte-for-byte regeneration checks. Asset bundles remain
140	  build outputs. Generator/tool selection still requires review.
141	  Retain required review evidence deliberately with its own custody;
142	  existing frozen evidence is not deleted or reorganized by this decision.
143	
144	## File inventory and naming conventions
145	
146	The user requested an explicit directory/filename list with a description of
147	what belongs in each file, including consistent names for similar
148	implementations. The [machine-readable inventory](repository-file-inventory.v1.json)
149	is the source for the generated tables below. Edit its entries and regenerate
150	this section; do not maintain a second handwritten list. Proposed files become
151	real as their implementation is needed, with the inventory updated whenever a
152	reviewed split, merge or rename changes their responsibilities.
153	
154	These are initial structural proposals. A listed filename does not establish
155	that its API, algorithm, dependency selection or product qualification is done.
156	This inventory deliberately leaves tool-specific build configuration and the
157	full schema migration map open until their owning decisions are made. Shared
158	platform behavior remains host-owned even when its code is in a support crate.
159	
160	### Naming rules
161	
162	| Category | Rust | TypeScript | Meaning |
163	|---|---|---|---|
164	| Ordinary source module | `snake_case.rs` | `kebab-case.ts` | Name the concrete responsibility; exported Rust types and TypeScript classes/types may use `PascalCase` |
165	| Factory | `<subject>_factory.rs` | `<subject>-factory.ts` | Select and construct an implementation from explicit inputs; do not hide workflow execution, discovery or permission grants in construction |
166	| Incremental builder | `<subject>_builder.rs` when a dedicated builder implementation exists | `<subject>-builder.ts` on the same rule | Incrementally construct a value; a function that constructs a descriptor can remain in its domain module |
167	| Named boundary adapter | `<boundary>_adapter.rs` | `<boundary>-adapter.ts` | Translate one named external boundary into owned structures; concrete platform mechanisms may retain names such as `filesystem.rs` |
168	| Renderer | `<format>_renderer.rs` | `<format>-renderer.ts` if one is needed | Produce a presentation of admitted data, without acquiring semantic authority |
169	| Persistent store implementation | `<subject>_store.rs` | `<subject>-store.ts` if one is needed | Own persistence mechanics; do not call browser view state a store of authoritative evidence |
170	| Generated bindings | `src/generated/<domain>.rs` | `src/generated/<domain>.ts` | Generated from the selected schema owner; never edited by hand |
171	| Separate behavioral test file | `<subject>_tests.rs` | `<subject>.test.ts` | Name the behavior or module under test; small Rust unit tests may remain inline |
172	
173	Standard ecosystem entrypoints keep their standard spelling: `Cargo.toml`,
174	`Cargo.lock`, `lib.rs`, `main.rs`, `mod.rs`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` and
175	`index.ts`. New JSON data filenames use kebab-case; schema documents use the
176	selected owner's schema/version spelling. Existing frozen artifacts are not
177	renamed to fit these implementation conventions. Folder names use kebab-case;
178	Rust source-module filenames use Rust's underscore convention.
179	
180	The three currently proposed factories are
181	`crates/components/src/session_factory.rs`,
182	`crates/reporting/src/renderer_factory.rs` and
183	`providers/typescript/src/program-factory.ts`. Their descriptions below state
184	which construction each owns. This convention does not require converting
185	ordinary constructors into factory abstractions.
186	
187	Use concrete domain names in preference to catch-all files such as `utils`,
188	`helpers`, `misc` or `manager`. If one of those names seems necessary, first
189	identify the actual responsibility and its owning package. Put browser-only
190	state in `view-state.ts`; transport types come from generated contracts rather
191	than a second handwritten `types.ts` containing unrelated records.
192	
193	### Ownership and dependency constraints
194	
195	Within the pure layers, `contracts` has no internal dependencies, `identity`
196	may depend on `contracts`, and `evaluator` may depend on `identity` and
197	`contracts`. Reversing those edges is forbidden even if the graph is acyclic.
198	These crates may also use explicitly reviewed pure external libraries.
199	They have no OS, provider, store or report UI dependency. Platform code supplies
200	mechanisms; security, lifecycle and host code decide whether an operation is
201	lawful. Host finalization coordinates the authoritative application boundary.
202	The [commit API proposal](implementation-boundaries-and-build-plan.md#admission-and-authoritative-commit)
203	requires storage's facade to consume opaque evaluator `ReplayedRun` and security
204	`CommitSession` prerequisites bound to the exact target; raw ledger mutation and
205	receipt constructors stay private to storage. Storage therefore gains direct
206	evaluator and security dependencies. An ordinary DTO or success flag cannot
207	substitute for those prerequisites. The exact carrier/recovery join is proposed
208	there for Claude review; no implemented type-level or durability guarantee is
209	claimed by this inventory.
210	
211	Components owns framing, negotiated protocol shape and session supervision.
212	Host fact admission owns the returned evidence's joins to the selected source,
213	context and Plan. Replay independently checks the semantic obligations over
214	explicitly supplied data. This keeps lifecycle's use of component management
215	from assigning it responsibility for analysis admission.
216	
217	The Rust provider is a separately pinned workspace. Its shared contract/identity
218	source dependencies must be resolved reproducibly without pulling its compiler
219	integration into the host workspace. The TypeScript provider and report are
220	separate packages. Both consume their selected generated bindings; neither
221	imports the other's runtime code. Report assets are supplied by build/release
222	assembly to host reporting, not by a runtime dependency on a web server.
223	
224	The source dependency graph alone does not describe these integration edges:
225	
226	| Relationship | Required boundary |
227	|---|---|
228	| Schemas → Rust contracts, TS provider and report bindings | Registry records exact source IDs/digests, profiles, generator version/options, generated targets and semantic validator owners; generated types alone do not perform runtime admission |
229	| Host components ↔ separately released providers | Negotiated process protocols and authenticated release closures; no source imports of compiler implementations into the host |
230	| Rust provider → shared Rust contract/identity libraries | Reproducible pinned dependency resolution within its separate workspace, explicit compatible toolchains and selected wire surfaces; a path dependency must not inherit incompatible root workspace settings |
231	| Report build → host reporting → CLI release | Versioned asset bundle matches the embedded projection and is included in the signed offline release closure; provider-only builds need no report toolchain |
232	| Shared fixtures → package tests and executable integration harnesses | Each scenario has an executable owner and an independent expected result; qualification evidence retains its separate standing |
233	
234	Root TypeScript scripts coordinate packages without making a combined frontend
235	build a prerequisite for provider development. A provider-side SDK is not yet
236	selected: compare shared transport obligations before adding a package. Common
237	host supervision, authorization and outcome behavior remains host-owned either
238	way. CLI bootstrap initializes only the services required by the admitted command;
239	static linkage does not justify opening stores or providers for help/version.
240	
241	Derived indexes belong to storage mechanics and have a lifecycle separate from
242	retained evidence. Host query owns exact Run/view selection, bounded traversal
243	and truthful completeness. Loss or interruption of an index leads to rebuilding,
244	a supported retained-evidence fallback or an explicit unavailable result under
245	the selected contract, never an invented empty answer. No graph engine is chosen.
246	
247	Current product semantics remain in the five product contracts. This inventory
248	maps those responsibilities onto prospective code; it does not change their
249	wire majors, typed outcomes or authority boundaries. In particular, the new
250	`schemas/` home needs an exact source/ID/generation mapping before migration;
251	this document does not silently replace the existing pinned schema files.
252	
253	The [inventory checker](../../operations/check_repository_file_inventory.py)
254	validates unique canonical paths, ownership, Rust/TypeScript naming, factory, store and
255	renderer suffixes, test names, generated-file locations, the pure-crate
256	dependency direction and an acyclic declared package graph. It also checks that this chapter matches the inventory. It does
257	not inspect an implemented dependency graph or prove semantic correctness.
258	Actual source/dependency enforcement belongs to the implementation's repository
259	checks once those files exist.
260	
261	```sh
262	python3 -I -B docs/operations/check_repository_file_inventory.py --write
263	python3 -I -B docs/operations/check_repository_file_inventory.py --check
264	```
265	
266	<!-- BEGIN GENERATED FILE INVENTORY -->
267	
268	### Proposed package boundaries
269	
270	Package names and dependency edges below are proposals except for the agreed
271	`opensip-cli` name. Non-Rust group IDs are inventory labels, not selected npm
272	package names. Dependencies list proposed direct Rust source edges;
273	generated-schema inputs, process protocols and asset delivery are separate
274	build/runtime relationships. This table grants no component authority.
275	
276	| Package/group | Directory | Responsibility | Proposed direct dependencies |
277	|---|---|---|---|
278	| `repository` | `./` | Workspace, contributor guidance and shared checks. | None declared |
279	| `opensip-cli` | `apps/cli/` | CLI parsing and application assembly. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-host` |
280	| `opensip-contracts` | `crates/contracts/` | Shared inert contract types and protocol declarations. | None declared |
281	| `opensip-identity` | `crates/identity/` | Pure canonical admission and content identity. | `opensip-contracts` |
282	| `opensip-evaluator` | `crates/evaluator/` | Pure policy evaluation and complete semantic reconstruction. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity` |
283	| `opensip-platform` | `crates/platform/` | OS mechanisms behind explicit interfaces, without policy authority. | `opensip-contracts` |
284	| `opensip-security` | `crates/security/` | Host trust, custody and authorization decisions. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity`, `opensip-platform` |
285	| `opensip-storage` | `crates/storage/` | Host-internal retained evidence mechanics. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity`, `opensip-evaluator`, `opensip-platform`, `opensip-security` |
286	| `opensip-components` | `crates/components/` | Common component negotiation and supervision. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity`, `opensip-platform` |
287	| `opensip-lifecycle` | `crates/lifecycle/` | Host installation and component generation lifecycle. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity`, `opensip-platform`, `opensip-security`, `opensip-components`, `opensip-storage` |
288	| `opensip-reporting` | `crates/reporting/` | Host-owned projections and output assembly. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity` |
289	| `opensip-host` | `crates/host/` | Application authority and complete workflow orchestration. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity`, `opensip-evaluator`, `opensip-platform`, `opensip-security`, `opensip-storage`, `opensip-components`, `opensip-lifecycle`, `opensip-reporting` |
290	| `typescript-provider` | `providers/typescript/` | Sealed-input TypeScript/JavaScript analysis; no host policy, storage or presentation authority. | None declared |
291	| `opensip-rust-provider` | `providers/rust/` | Independently pinned Rust compiler/provider integration. | `opensip-contracts`, `opensip-identity` |
292	| `report` | `apps/report/` | Build offline browser report assets; no provider or host runtime import. | None declared |

296	| `product-docs` | `docs/` | One current implementation reading path with linked historical evidence. | None declared |
297	
298	### Proposed filenames and responsibilities
299	
300	The inventory currently contains **190 proposed files**. Each
301	row names one target file. Generated rows are owned outputs of schema
302	generation; their schemas and semantic validators remain distinct owners.
303	This is a planning inventory, not an instruction to create empty files.
304

18	## Admission and authoritative commit
19	
20	### Decision: require independently minted prerequisites at the storage boundary
21	
22	A private host wrapper alone cannot prevent another Rust caller of a public
23	storage crate from submitting unverified records. Select two opaque prerequisites:
24	the pure evaluator produces a **ReplayedRun**, and security produces a live
25	**CommitSession**. Storage can publish an authoritative commit only with both,
26	bound to the same exact target. Host finalization remains the application
27	coordinator; it does not manufacture either prerequisite from booleans or DTOs.
28	
29	This changes the proposed source graph: `opensip-storage` depends directly on
30	`opensip-evaluator` and `opensip-security`, in addition to contracts, identity
31	and platform. Neither evaluator nor security depends on storage. Lifecycle may
32	continue to use storage without a reverse storage → lifecycle edge. The evaluator
33	remains entirely pure; being called by effectful storage does not give it ports,
34	callbacks or access to live state. The dependency/footprint tradeoff is explicit
35	and requires Claude review. Do not create an extra admission crate merely to
36	hide this edge or weaken full replay to keep a diagram smaller.
37	
38	These are proposed Rust API type names, not new serialized contracts:
39	
40	| Type / operation | Constructor and visibility | Invariant |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| `RunCandidate` | Inert contract input; callers may construct/deserialize it | Makes no admission claim |
43	| `ReplayedRun` | Public opaque evaluator type; constructor private to complete replay in `replay.rs` | Contains exact admitted closure, recomputed RunId, retention inventory and selected profile after full semantic reconstruction; no `Default`, deserialization or unchecked constructor |
44	| `CommitSession` | Public opaque security type; created only by security admission over registered project/store custody, an owned live platform writer guard, actual grants and operation identity | Binds namespace, store generation, ExecutionId, admitted producer closure and permitted operation; acquisition never follows from a Run's semantic grant projection |
45	| `PreparedCommit` | Public opaque storage type; returned by `prepare_commit(ReplayedRun, CommitSession)` | Owns both prerequisites and the exact binding; checks equality and retention feasibility, then permits only the defined publication sequence |
46	| `PublishedCommit` | Public opaque storage result; constructor private to durable commit/recovery validation | Contains the exact committed receipt and Run reference after required barriers, not merely after writing blobs or appending SEAL |
47	| `RecoveredCommit` | Storage recovery result validated against current ledger and objects | Distinguishes confirmed commit, confirmed absence/failure and an inability to establish either; recovery does not repeat source mutation |

49	Owned guards and commit state are single-use and non-cloneable. Immutable byte
50	buffers may be shared read-only; the opaque wrapper exposes no mutable interior
51	or references that let a caller replace a validated object. An owned byte arena
52	or pinned read-only verified object set can avoid copying the entire closure;
53	filesystem paths alone cannot freeze it. Accessors provide identities and
54	read-only values, never a way to construct the prerequisite. Test helpers that
55	skip admission remain private to unit tests and unavailable in release builds.
56	
57	`ReplayedRun` establishes semantic validity, not compiler truth, present custody
58	or current availability. `CommitSession` establishes operational admission, not
59	semantic validity. Storage compares their target identities, inventories and
60	producer selections, binds the current attempt and verifies all published bytes.
61	Changed Plan inputs require new replay. A new attempt using the same semantic
62	Run still requires a new session and its own ExecutionId/receipt.
63	
64	The storage crate exports read APIs, cache/index APIs, authorized maintenance
65	APIs and the guarded commit facade. SQL connections, transaction handles,
66	ledger-row insertion and receipt constructors remain private modules. Host,
67	lifecycle and CLI cannot obtain raw writable ledger access through a convenience
68	method. Maintenance cannot insert an authoritative Run by using a restore or
69	migration helper: imported evidence is revalidated before local adoption, and
70	state transitions retain their separate authorization and recovery laws.

72	This is an API discipline inside the trusted host, not an OS sandbox or a
73	defense against arbitrary malicious native code running with store access.
74	Custody, exact-byte admission and actual platform qualification remain necessary.

76	### Publication sequence and lock discipline
77	
78	1. Host obtains registered project/store admission and the required writer guard
79	   through lifecycle/security before source admission. The guard remains owned
80	   through evaluation and commit. Operational grants precede Plan construction;
81	   Plan grant descriptors never authorize effects.
82	2. Native/import admission and the pure evaluator reconstruct the complete Run.
83	   A failed reconstruction returns its typed failure without producing
84	   `ReplayedRun`. Explicit ephemeral analysis uses a separate non-authoritative
85	   result path and cannot call the durable commit facade.
86	3. Storage binds the two prerequisites and preflights exact replayable retention,
87	   pins and bounds. It writes verified immutable objects to private temporary
88	   files, satisfies file barriers, publishes digest-addressed objects and
89	   satisfies directory barriers. Failure leaves no acknowledged Run.
90	4. Prepare both carrier write transactions at level 3 in one fixed order:
91	   security grant-journal first, evidence ledger second, both non-waiting. If
92	   either acquisition fails, release the earlier transaction. Only then take
93	   the journal append checkpoint at level 4. It never holds level 4 while
94	   trying to acquire either level-3 transaction. No lease upgrade or new project/fence
95	   acquisition occurs inside this path. Existing S7 rules own earlier fence and
96	   lease acquisition/release and contention handling.
97	5. Under the journal checkpoint, security checks current custody, relevant trust
98	   epoch, observer freshness, grants and operation cancellation. The final
99	   SEAL/commit sequence must linearize with REV: no new SEAL or commit after REV.
100	   No slow replay, provider execution, network operation or discovery occurs
101	   while this final lock is held. A short-lived checkpoint is never serialized
102	   as a reusable authority token.
103	6. Publish the Run manifest, references, availability, authorized pins, exact
104	   receipt and private recovery association in one synchronous ledger
105	   transaction; satisfy all required durability barriers. Only then produce
106	   `PublishedCommit`. Required rendering/delivery follows commitment and cannot
107	   rewrite its Run.
108	
109	**Proposed journal/ledger crash join for review:** persist the validated SEAL
110	record before ledger commit while holding the final journal lock through the
111	ledger commit/barrier. Include a private recovery association in that ledger
112	transaction linking namespace, ExecutionId, RunId, inventory digest, store
113	generation and the exact journal generation/sequence/record digest. Its values
114	come from the actual two owners, not caller assertions. The association is local
115	operational metadata, excluded from semantic hashes, and adds no field to the
116	closed public receipt or JournalRecord schemas. SEAL alone is not a durable
117	receipt. A surviving SEAL with no committed ledger row is an uncommitted attempt.
118	
119	This is a concrete proposed carrier join, not a claim that candidate25 already
120	specifies or implements that private table. Claude must check its compatibility
121	with the selected journal carrier, operationRef binding, recovery and bounded
122	revocation rules. The private record shape and ordered fault-injection plan below now make the
123	proposal concrete. Their carrier implementation/migration still requires review
124	and real execution before qualification.
125	If that review requires a normative amendment, freeze and review a successor;
126	do not silently edit the selected public schemas or weaken the existing laws.

128	### Failure and recovery account
129	
130	| Interruption / refusal | Durable state and required behavior |
131	|---|---|
132	| Invalid closure or semantic mismatch | No replay prerequisite; no acknowledged Run or fabricated commit receipt |
133	| Wrong namespace/store generation, substituted Run/inventory or expired operational session | Refuse before authoritative publication; never repair the mismatch by rebinding an existing token |
134	| Object write/digest/barrier failure | No ledger commit; unreferenced blobs are reconciled under existing GC/custody rules |
135	| REV/cancellation/freshness failure before commit | Prevent subsequent SEAL/commit according to S6; disclose already completed effects under their own rules |
136	| Durable SEAL, ledger transaction not committed | No authoritative acknowledgement; recovery requires verified ledger absence before calling the attempt uncommitted; a read failure is not absence |
137	| Commit/barrier result uncertain, or acknowledgement lost | Return the existing durability-undetermined outcome with ExecutionId; read-only recovery checks the ledger, binding and objects; no automatic mutation retry |
138	| Receipt confirms commit, later object loss/corruption | Preserve historical sealed assurance and verdict; report current availability and missing references separately |
139	| Required report projection/rendering fails after commit | Preserve RunId; existing required-delivery operational failure/exit 4 applies |
140	| Optional browser launch/export fails | Disclose the optional delivery failure according to the selected surface; do not change the sealed result |
141	
142	Recovery must not use a lone SEAL, a matching cache key or a syntactically valid
143	RunId as proof of commitment. Conversely, revocation after a confirmed commit
144	does not erase history. Corrupt or contradictory operational records require
145	an honest recovery/custody failure under the owning error contract; this design
146	does not invent a new public error code to conceal an unmapped case.

205	### Witness-aware publication and read-only recovery
206	
207	The inherited security v8 §5.4 witness protocol is part of the carrier boundary.
208	Final SEAL publication must complete its **PENDING witness → journal transaction
209	commit/barrier → COMMITTED witness** sequence before the evidence-ledger commit.
210	The broad journal record schema's i64 `seq` allowance does not override the
211	carrier's uint53 cap or reserved terminal slot: ordinary SEAL uses at most
212	`9007199254740990`; slot `9007199254740991` remains TERMINAL. Capacity handling
213	must finish through lifecycle outside the held operation lease, never by taking
214	its fence backwards inside commit.
215	
216	The inherited `security-schemas.v2/grant-journal.sql` does not admit SEAL in its
217	record-type CHECK and still names historical platform aliases. It is historical
218	carrier evidence, not ready-to-use product DDL. **COV-03** requires an explicitly
219	versioned product carrier migration that admits current schema-3 SEAL/current
220	platform records while preserving historical row interpretation, append-only
221	hash chains, reserved capacity, witness/high-water checks and the S9 reader/core
222	bridge. Do not disable SQL checks or relabel old rows as current. A journal's own
223	SQLite transaction is distinct from the evidence ledger transaction; holding
224	the prescribed lock order does not make the two databases atomically committed.
225	The proposal orders both level-3 write transactions before the level-4 append
226	lock: grant journal, then evidence ledger. Every journal writer, including the
227	revocation observer, must use the same security-owned transaction-before-append
228	API; no caller may acquire a new journal transaction from inside an append-lock
229	callback. A failed second acquisition rolls back/releases the first. Committing
230	the journal releases its DB transaction while the append lock stays held through
231	the witness and evidence commit; no journal transaction is reacquired there.
232	Claude must review this refinement against S7 and every inherited journal writer.
233	
234	Read-only recovery may inspect a consistent ledger snapshot and the admitted
235	carrier/witness/floor state. It must not perform witness INIT, REVERT or ADVANCE,
236	raise trust high-water, allocate a store binding or obtain a new execution grant.
237	If reconciliation of the requested attempt's carrier prefix is needed, report
238	the owner diagnosis and inability to confirm current local custody; an
239	authorized lifecycle open performs the lawful mutation,
240	then a new read-only recovery can retry. A mere absent or malformed witness never
241	licenses repair. The ordinary writer lifecycle's existing start/end high-water
242	handoff stays separate from a read-only request.
243	
244	A journal tail ahead of the witness, a missing witness for nonempty history,
245	a lower-than-observed tail, an equal sequence with different hash, unknown schema
246	or contradictory receipt/association is a custody/recovery refusal. A verified
247	empty exact ledger lookup can establish that an attempt did not commit; an
248	unreadable ledger, another generation, the requested attempt still running or
249	an unresolved witness for its required prefix cannot. Active-attempt recovery
250	may report in-progress/undetermined and must not declare a final failure from an
251	older read snapshot. A valid later append's PENDING witness does not invalidate
252	an earlier committed receipt: snapshot readers verify its retained durable
253	prefix and never wait for the writer or repair the newer witness. Ordinary
254	historical queries do not reuse current execution grants or turn each read into
255	whole-carrier recovery.
256	
257	Preserve the recovery association, exact receipt, store-generation lineage and
258	required journal verification material while their local commitment is retained.
259	They are operational custody state under G19, not disposable indexes. Removing
260	or compacting a journal generation requires an explicitly reviewed retained
261	verification bridge; absence of that bridge prevents deletion. This proposal
262	does not alter immutable assurance or claim that purge deletes exported copies.
263	
264	Before ledger commit, recheck observer freshness/cancellation after any blocking
265	journal/witness operation. SEAL may already be durable; a failed final checkpoint
266	latches fail-stop and rolls back the still-uncommitted evidence transaction.
267	Release the append lock and remaining transaction/operation resources in the
268	specified order before a fresh lawful journal append records REV/cleanup; never
269	reacquire a level-3 journal transaction under level 4. No further effect is
270	admitted from the failed session. The old SEAL remains an uncommitted attempt. The journal lock
271	orders REV against commit; it cannot bound an OS syscall stalled indefinitely.
272	S6 scheduling assumptions and real platform measurements remain required.

339	### Required API and fault-injection checks
340	
341	`crates/host/tests/admission_tests.rs` owns public-boundary scenarios;
342	`crates/storage/tests/commit_tests.rs` owns the real carrier crash matrix;
343	private evaluator/security unit tests own prerequisite construction. Verify:
344	
345	- Raw DTOs, a boolean `verified`, structural-only validation and a serialized
346	  previous session cannot enter the commit facade. Include compile-fail API
347	  fixtures once the test harness is selected, plus behavioral rejection checks.
348	- Alter any admitted input, inventory, namespace, execution or generation at
349	  the handoff; no acknowledged authority results. Exercise live revocation and
350	  stale-guard behavior with deterministic synchronization.
351	- Interrupt before/after every object barrier, SEAL append/barrier, ledger
352	  transaction/barrier and acknowledgement. Recover in a fresh process using
353	  actual stored bytes; distinguish orphan, committed and indeterminate states.
354	- Concurrent readers see a consistent committed snapshot; a competing writer
355	  or exclusive operation follows S7 contention rules without a reversed lock
356	  acquisition. Releasing an object drops guards in the specified order.
357	- An identity-valid but replay-invalid candidate never publishes authority.
358	  Loss of report assets after commitment does not change its evidence or verdict.

360	These are required future implementation checks, not tests run in this design
361	task. Reference-model success cannot establish OS durability or process isolation.

363	## Build, generation and dependency rules
364	
365	### Independently selectable build lanes
366	
367	| Lane | Source roots and prerequisites | Output / isolation requirement |
368	|---|---|---|
369	| Host libraries and CLI development | Root Cargo workspace: `apps/cli` and selected `crates/*`; root lockfile/toolchain | Native host and package tests; neither provider compiler integration nor Node/report build is an implicit Cargo build-script prerequisite |
370	| Rust provider | Separate `providers/rust` workspace, lockfile and toolchain; exact shared pure library sources | Provider executable plus its declared runtime/compiler/standard-library assets; host build does not compile rustc integration |
371	| TypeScript provider | Its own TS package and pinned compiler/runtime dependencies | Provider executable/launch payload and sealed runtime closure; no browser/report imports or frontend build requirement |
372	| Browser report | `apps/report` and generated projection binding | Self-contained asset bundle and compatibility descriptor; no provider or host runtime imports |
373	| Contract generation | Selected schema source registry and pinned generator closure | Rust/TS carriers and runtime validators; deterministic drift check across all declared consumers |
374	| Product release assembly | Explicitly chosen native binaries, report assets, providers, storage and trust inputs | Signed exact offline closure and compatibility/TCB inventory; source directory adjacency does not establish compatibility |
375	
376	The default product release remains authoritative-capable. A management-only
377	installation is explicit and refuses analysis until its required signed closure
378	is installed through the authorized lifecycle. Optional development build lanes
379	must not become a new preview product, silently omit required capabilities from
380	a release, or download missing tools at runtime.
381	
382	**Rust workspace policy.** Shared pure packages must be usable from the pinned
383	provider workspace without accidentally inheriting the root workspace's compiler
384	or dependency settings. Their distributable manifests explicitly resolve package
385	metadata and dependencies; source-package assembly may materialize inherited
386	values, but the isolated provider build must prove they resolve without the host
387	workspace. Each workspace's lockfile is authoritative for that build. Shared
388	library/API compatibility, each wire major and toolchain support are separate
389	axes; a new host release does not force a provider release. Build inputs may
390	include immutable exported source packages from the one owner; never maintain
391	editable provider copies of shared contracts.
392	
393	**TypeScript policy.** Root scripts may coordinate the provider and report, but
394	must expose independent build/test targets. Select one package manager and
395	lockfile strategy before scaffolding; do not check in competing lockfiles. A
396	shared lockfile is acceptable only if each lane can install/build its declared
397	closure without running the other's scripts or requiring its toolchain. Provider
398	Node and browser DOM environments have separate compiler settings. Runtime
399	imports, type-only imports and generated inputs all appear in dependency checks;
400	type-only imports cannot hide duplicate schema ownership.
401	
402	**Generation policy.** Select checked-in generated bindings for the initial
403	implementation: ordinary builds can consume reviewed bindings without running a
404	generator or fetching schemas. Generated headers identify their owner and recipe;
405	the registry pins source digest/ID/profile, generator version/closure and options,
406	output target and semantic validator owner. The generation lane regenerates into
407	a clean temporary directory and compares bytes with the checked-in outputs.
408	Changes to a source/recipe must update every affected consumer in the same change.
409	Only explicit registry membership determines outputs; no glob over historical
410	schema versions. Generators must not resolve remote references implicitly.
411	
412	**Asset policy.** Generated JS/CSS bundles and release binaries are build outputs,
413	not checked-in application source. Report assembly emits a manifest of exact
414	asset bytes, projection compatibility and license/notice inputs. The host consumes
415	that manifest through an explicit build/release input; a Cargo build script must
416	not invoke an ambient package manager or contact the network. A source build can
417	use locally built assets; a verified prebuilt bundle is another explicit input.
418	Development host tests may use labelled fixture assets. A product release must
419	fail assembly if its selected report asset closure is missing or incompatible.
420	Rendering a required output fails honestly if the installed assets are unusable.
421	
422	### Enforcement and verification
423	
424	1. Compare actual direct Cargo normal/build/dev dependencies, target-conditioned
425	   edges and activated features with the inventory's permitted graph. Record
426	   dev-only exceptions explicitly; do not silently broaden a production edge.
427	   Inspect transitive effects/build scripts of pure-layer external libraries.
428	2. Check TS imports and package exports against provider/browser boundaries.
429	   Check scripts and generation/asset edges as well as import graphs. Detect
430	   reverse edges, undeclared sibling source imports and provider toolchains
431	   entering the host's build closure.
432	3. Build each lane from a clean input manifest with dependencies materialized
433	   beforehand; an offline rebuild must not fetch missing inputs. Record source,
434	   lockfile, compiler, generator, platform and asset identities. Do not claim
435	   bit-for-bit reproducibility until measured; deterministic findings and
436	   reproducible release binaries are different properties.
437	4. Assemble each advertised product profile from exact compatible artifacts and
438	   test installation/analysis with blocked egress. Record mandatory and incremental
439	   sizes, help/version startup, memory and actual loader dependencies under the
440	   existing qualification gates; importing a pure crate is not a size measurement.
441	5. Run independent schema/protocol/output conformance vectors, built-browser
442	   offline/accessibility checks and real process/storage failure scenarios.
443	   A root `tests/` README links executable owners; it is not an executable harness.
444	
445	The pending tool choice list is finite: supported toolchain versions, TS package
446	manager/lock layout, frontend/bundler, schema generator/runtime-validator tool,
447	dependency checker, browser/compile-fail/OS harnesses, and release adapter.
448	Select them against these rules and existing qualification requirements before
449	the corresponding implementation milestone. This document does not adopt the
450	prototype's framework, dependency versions or lockstep release train by default.

3	**Standing: source-inspected author proposal, 2026-09-11; actual Claude review pending.**
4	
5	This is the single current inventory of prototype report features and their
6	proposed migration dispositions. [Chapter 14](14-repository-and-module-layout.md)
7	owns file locations; the [implementation plan](implementation-boundaries-and-build-plan.md)
8	owns API/build/milestone decisions. A “Preserve” or “Change” row is proposed
9	design scope, not an implemented or independently accepted parity claim.

11	## Evidence and limits
12	
13	The sibling prototype checkout is clean at the already pinned commit `a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0`.
14	The inventory inspects its host report composition, dashboard generator, browser
15	modules and selected test sources. File bytes and selected architectural source
16	digests are recorded in [planning sources](implementation-planning-sources.v1.json).
17	Links below resolve to that exact prototype commit, not its moving main branch.

19	This review did not execute the prototype, run its test suite, measure browser
20	performance or visually qualify accessibility. Test names are evidence of intended
21	coverage, not a passing result. Source comments describing earlier measurements

171	## Proposed implementation owners and acceptance
172	
173	| Responsibility | Owning target modules | Required evidence |
174	|---|---|---|
175	| Common projection, data validation and offline assembly | Reporting projection/html_embedding/assets; report report-data and generated binding | Applicable parity, hostile text, unknown/incompatible payloads, no network fetches, required failure propagation |
176	| Overview, historical selection and catalogs | Report overview-view, history-view and catalog-view; host query/configuration | Exact IDs and history scope, missing evidence states, admissible catalog provenance |
177	| Findings, evidence and audit | Report findings-view, evidence-view and comparison-view | Complete required fields, baseline attribution, runtime/import limitations and honest incomplete results |
178	| Graph and symbol exploration | Report graph-view and symbol-detail-view; host query and reporting projection | Exact occurrence identities, bounded relationship/path results, no client-derived policy or global absence claim |
179	| Navigation, help and exports | Report navigation, help-view and exports | Keyboard/focus behavior, safe routes/schemes, formula-safe local download, no analysis or mutation effects |
180	| Publication and optional opening | Host delivery and platform process/filesystem | Atomic artifact output, correct after-commit failures, no launch in disallowed contexts |
181	
182	These browser modules are additions to the canonical filename inventory, not
183	new applications or providers. Sorting, fuzzy search and layout can be browser
184	presentation functions over embedded data. Any browser-computed subset statistic
185	must be labelled as such; semantic paths, completeness, verdicts and required
186	parity values come from the host projection. No client-side operation can obtain
187	new repository evidence or promote a display result to an authoritative finding.
188	
189	## Explicit migration boundaries
190	
191	- The prototype includes heuristic browser tracing and body-hash lookups. Their
192	  useful navigation is retained through exact identities and host evidence, not
193	  by reproducing those algorithms as authoritative analysis.
194	- The old shared graph filter drawer is not a retained feature: its source says
195	  it was removed. Current visualization owns its controls; other views use their
196	  own filters. Avoid restoring obsolete UI based on filenames alone.
197	- A report is an offline snapshot. Its availability observations describe the
198	  recorded observation time/generation; opening the file tomorrow does not learn
199	  whether the live store was purged. Fresh availability requires a new admitted
200	  host query/report, with explicit identity and observation provenance.
201	- Required HTML supports the selected analysis and query surfaces. The full
202	  embedded projection and schema mapping must be designed from the final output
203	  contract before UI implementation. These feature rows do not add arbitrary
204	  fields to closed CommandEnvelope schemas or advertise a new report command.
205	- Graph display budgets, browser limits and package-size targets need measured
206	  acceptance thresholds. Do not inherit the prototype’s 8 MiB graph budget or
207	  its history caps as product law. They are useful cases for the measurement plan.
208	- Visual styling, frontend framework, graph library and exact legacy simulation
209	  UI remain separate choices. No feature is silently dropped: R24 proposes a
210	  deferral requiring explicit disposition in the actual review.

2	"""Check source-bound planning coverage and render its owning document.
3	
4	This validates design bookkeeping, not product behavior or qualification.
5	Use --source for the materialized candidate25 snapshot. --write changes only
6	the two generated sections in the implementation plan; no product scaffolding.
7	"""
8	import argparse
9	import hashlib
10	import json
11	import re
12	from pathlib import Path
13	
14	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
15	ARCH = ROOT / "docs/v2/architecture"
16	PLAN = ARCH / "implementation-boundaries-and-build-plan.md"
17	
18	
19	def require(condition, message):
20	    if not condition:
21	        raise ValueError(message)
22	
23	
24	def sha(data):
25	    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
26	
27	
28	def digest(value):
29	    return sha(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
30	                          ensure_ascii=False).encode())
31	
32	
33	def load(path):
34	    return json.loads(path.read_text())
35	
36	
37	def section_values(text):
38	    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
39	    heads = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line.startswith("## ")]
40	    return [(i + 1, {"heading": lines[start].strip(), "firstLine": start + 1,
41	                     "lastLine": end}, "".join(lines[start:end]))
42	            for i, (start, end) in enumerate(zip(heads, heads[1:] + [len(lines)]))]
43	
44	
45	def expected_groups(sources):
46	    result = {}
47	
48	    def rows(group, key, values, id_fn, prefix):
49	        result[group] = {id_fn(v): (key, f"{prefix}/{i}", v)
50	                         for i, v in enumerate(values)}
51	
52	    commands = sources["commands"]
53	    rows("commands", "commands", commands["commands"], lambda x: x["name"], "/commands")
54	    rows("sharedFlags", "commands", commands["sharedFlags"], lambda x: x["flag"], "/sharedFlags")
55	    rows("renderers", "commands", commands["renderers"], lambda x: x["format"], "/renderers")
56	    rows("workflowGoldens", "commands", commands["goldens"], lambda x: x["id"], "/goldens")
57	    rows("queryOperations", "query", sources["query"]["$defs"]["Operation"]["enum"],
58	         lambda x: x, "/$defs/Operation/enum")
59	    rows("capabilityCells", "nativeMatrix", sources["nativeMatrix"]["cells"],
60	         lambda x: x["capability"] + "/" + x["mode"], "/cells")
61	    rows("qualificationGates", "gates", sources["gates"]["items"], lambda x: x["id"], "/items")
62	    result["contractSections"] = {}

64	                "workflows-and-surfaces", "admission-and-qualification"):
65	        for i, selector, value in section_values(sources[key]):
66	            result["contractSections"][key + ":" + str(i)] = (key, selector, value)
67	    result["fallowConstraints"] = {}

303	Trust floors are excluded from lifecycle backups and generation rollback; any declared restore marks

312	denial where it is detected or declared, and at most formerly valid authority, aging into denial,

421	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
422	
423	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
424	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
425	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
426	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
427	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
428	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
429	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
430	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
431	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
432	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
433	stops before any further effect.
434	
435	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
436	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
437	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
438	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
439	
440	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
441	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
442	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
443	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
444	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
445	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
446	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
447	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
448	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
449	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
450	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
451	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
452	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
453	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.
454	
455	**Three different SEAL boundaries, not one.** (1) `linearize` is an abstract
456	brokered-effect schedule over a grant journal. Its all-zero `run3:` SEAL id is
457	a **fixture** token for that schedule. It is not a product host, not native
458	fact authority, and not `identity-model.v3.close_run`. (2)
459	`admit_seal_run_id_prefix` is narrow `run3` pattern dispatch. It admits a
460	well-formed non-fixture prefix and refuses `run2` and the fixture id. It does
461	not replay a graph. (3) `admit_analysis_seal` is the public reference SEAL of
462	an analysis Run: current `JournalRecord` fields (`recordSchema` 3, closed
463	required members), then `identity-model.v3.close_run` on the supplied retained
464	graph, then byte-equal RunId comparison. Owner-only `open_run_closure` is not
465	that boundary. A well-formed `run3:` that is not the replayed identity refuses
466	`SEAL_RUN_ID_MISMATCH`. Schema-2 journals remain frozen historical bytes and
467	are not read as 3. Mixed prefixes refuse. There is no `run[23]` alternation.
468	Revocation still blocks schedule-SEAL after `REV`. Grant/root schema-2
469	documents are a different axis. This dispatch does not change lease modes,
470	lock order, or permission-truth-table effect values. Proof
471	`executionInputsDigest` is required by identity reconstruct; this unit does
472	not mint it.
473	
474	## S7. Leases and lock order (AR-14)
475	
476	The current security schema bundle declares every array's `x-opensip-order`
477	under identity §3. Namespace lists use strictly unique raw UTF-8 locator order;
478	execution-grant owner records use strictly unique `ownerKey` order. Public code
479	sets use strictly unique UTF-8 order. Other arrays are explicit sequences unless
480	their owning schema states a stricter order: journal revisions, lock traces,
481	release steps, signature entries and observations are never silently sorted.
482	This collection-admission law does not change the security metadata canonical
483	profile or its immutable historical schemas.
484	
485	| Level | Lock | Carrier | Blocking |
486	|---|---|---|---|
487	| 0 | lifecycle fence | `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`, flock LOCK_EX | bounded wait 5 s, then `PROJECT.BUSY` |
488	| 1 | project writer lease | `<namespace>/writer.lease`, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB | never |
489	| 2 | project reader lease | `<namespace>/readers.lease`, LOCK_SH\|LOCK_NB (readers); LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB (EXCLUSIVE) | never |
490	| 3 | ledger transaction | SQLite WAL; writers BEGIN IMMEDIATE, busy_timeout 0; readers read a committed snapshot | never for readers |
491	| 4 | journal append lock | in-process mutex | bounded, in-process |
492	
493	Modes: `SHARED-READ` (any number; queries, rendering, doctor, read-only
494	agents), `APPEND-WRITE` (one; analysis, import, baseline pin; publishes only
495	new immutable objects and ledger rows, never deletes or rewrites bytes a reader
496	may reference), `EXCLUSIVE` (GC, purge, migration, repair apply; nothing else
497	held). Readers never block a writer; a second writer or an EXCLUSIVE request
498	gets `PROJECT.BUSY` at once, releases the fence, and may retry outside the
499	fence with backoff 1/2/4/8/15 s within a 30 s budget. Laws: no lease without
500	the fence; no waiting for a lease; no waiting for the fence while holding a
501	lease (operation end releases the lease first); no upgrade; trust state is
502	written only under the fence and never under a lease; GC census is a
503	LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe under the fence and a busy probe means retain.
504	
505	**One-writer refinement (identity-and-evidence §5).** "Exactly one per-project
506	writer holds the lifecycle lease through admission, evaluation and commit" is
507	the APPEND-WRITE mode: exactly one append writer, coexisting with any number of
508	immutable-snapshot readers that never wait on it. The EXCLUSIVE mode is the
509	refinement for migration, purge, GC and repair apply, which need a reader
510	census (the LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe) because they may remove or rewrite bytes a
511	reader could reference. There is no contradiction with the identity contract:
512	readers are invisible to the writer's commit order and the writer is invisible
513	to readers' snapshots. Exact selectors: `<namespace>/writer.lease` LOCK_EX|NB
514	is the identity contract's "lifecycle lease"; `<namespace>/readers.lease`
515	LOCK_SH|NB is its "consistent committed snapshot"; `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`
516	is its "global trust admission and revocation lock order".
517	
518	**Namespaces.** Every project lease names a namespace from the host namespace
519	registry (ProjectId ↔ namespace locator, identity §5); a lease on an
520	unregistered namespace is a violation, never an implicit registration
521	(`lease-on-an-unregistered-namespace-is-refused-negative`). Namespaces are
522	independent: a writer in one never blocks a writer in another.
523	
524	**Core-transition lock set (decided; SHOULD-6).** `core update|repair|rollback`
525	and `store migrate|rollback` change install-level state, while EXCLUSIVE is a
526	per-namespace lease. The mechanism is a composition, not a new flock mode:
527	
528	1. The install-wide fence (level 0) is held for the **whole** transition, not
529	   only for lease acquisition; no project operation can be admitted meanwhile.
530	2. The affected namespace set is enumerated from the registry by
531	   `core_transition_affected_namespaces` (never from user input or a directory
532	   listing): **all registered namespaces** when the from/to state schema differ
533	   or a store is re-selected (`core rollback`, `store migrate|rollback`);
534	   **no namespace** for a same-schema `core update` or `core repair`, because
535	   the selected core closure is an immutable generation, running project
536	   operations keep their pinned generation and re-check trust at their S6
537	   checkpoints, and nothing they reference is rewritten.
538	3. EXCLUSIVE is taken on each affected namespace in namespace-locator byte
539	   order, non-blocking and all-or-nothing: the first busy namespace releases
540	   every acquired lease in reverse order, releases the fence, reports
541	   `PROJECT.BUSY` naming that namespace and its holders, and the retry is the
542	   ordinary backoff outside the fence.
543	4. The `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` (S9.2) names the exact lease set and is
544	   written only after every lease is held: in the lock model the
545	   `transition-journal` action is lawful only under the fence, only after
546	   `core-transition-acquire` succeeded, and only naming exactly the held set
547	   (`transition-journal-*` cases). Crash
548	   recovery runs as the first act under the next fence acquisition, before any
549	   admission, over the S9.2 recovery table (which defers to the S9 footprint
550	   table for store operations), and re-acquires exactly the journaled
551	   set; flock leases die with the process, so no stale lease survives. A
552	   namespace registered after the intent cannot exist (registration needs the
553	   fence); finding one is `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`.
554	5. Leases are released in reverse order, then the fence. The fence cannot be
555	   released while transition leases are held.
556	
557	Ordinary component `install`/`update` publish new immutable generations under
558	the fence alone and never revoke a generation a live operation pins (removal
559	is GC census only). GC iterates registered namespaces and treats a busy
560	namespace as retain, never as refusal. Reference `lease_schedule` (registry,
561	`core-transition-acquire|release`, `transition-journal`),
562	`core_transition_affected_namespaces`; cases `core-transition-*`,
563	`transition-journal-*`, `two-namespaces-are-independent-*`.
564	
565	Command → lease map (workflows command inventory):
566	
567	| Lease | Commands |
568	|---|---|
569	| none (fence only, no project lock) | `install`, `update` (component generations), `trust refresh|import|recovery-challenge|recovery-import`, ordinary payload import, `doctor` / `trust doctor` / `store status` (report-only, no write) |
570	| SHARED-READ | `query`, `recommend`, `baseline show`, `policy show|test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview`, `agent serve` reads, `doctor` project checks |
571	| APPEND-WRITE | `opensip` default, `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `test run`, `native prepare`, `repair verify` |
572	| EXCLUSIVE (one namespace) | `repair apply` (S10.1 authorization), `repair recover --apply-recovery` (S10.2 authorization; inspection alone is SHARED-READ), `purge`, `store gc` per namespace (busy = retain) |
573	| core-transition lock set (fence held + EXCLUSIVE on every affected registered namespace) | `core update`, `core repair`, `core rollback`, `store migrate`, `store rollback` |
574	
575	Trust recovery deliberately takes no project lease: it mutates SC-TRUST only,
576	under the fence, and a project operation that starts afterwards observes the
577	new floor at its trust instant.

1	# Proposed resolutions from the additional author audit
2	
3	Standing: Codex author proposals against candidate25. These are concrete review
4	inputs, not accepted replacements or an applied successor. Historical schemas,
5	review receipts and candidate25 bytes remain unchanged.
6	
7	## XA-01 — count selected project directories after boundary selection
8	
9	Security S3 and native §1.4 must apply the 4096-directory admission limit after
10	nested-authority and custody exclusions, and after explicit workspace-root
11	selection. An unrelated directory outside that selection cannot reject it.
12	A directory with co-located language markers counts once. Cargo member roots
13	retained by the existing explicit-workspace folding rule remain selected input
14	directories; this change does not remove member semantics or change later Plan
15	bounds. The refusal must publish the actual selected count and limit, with no
16	partial successful unit set.
17	
18	The three-file reference proposal implements this ordering in a separate copy.
19	The shared enumerator keeps its existing default cap for standalone callers;
20	security and native composition defer that cap until their selection is known.
21	This is a reference correction to the existing exclusion/override promise.
22	It does not implement a filesystem scanner or qualify its work bounds.
23	
24	## XA-02 — disclose observed counts without requiring hidden-tree enumeration
25	
26	Replace S3's promise to report the number of hidden markers with this rule:
27	
28	> Record each encountered pruned directory anchor once without descending into
29	> it to enumerate markers. A marker count is an observation over an explicitly
30	> supplied inventory, never a claim about unenumerated contents. Production
31	> discovery may report the count as unknown. A separately admitted native
32	> dependency read set does not retroactively make discovery exhaustive.
33	
34	The proposed successor row is closed:
35	`{path, reason, markerCount, markerCountBasis}`. `path`/`reason` keep their
36	existing meanings. `markerCountBasis` is `not-enumerated` or `observed-inventory`.
37	For `not-enumerated`, `markerCount` is null. For `observed-inventory`, it is a
38	nonnegative exact integer counting distinct supplied marker paths under that
39	anchor, with no assertion of filesystem totality. Zero observed is not zero
40	hidden. The bounded host directory observation supplies pruned anchors even
41	when no descendant marker is observed. Native composition consumes those
42	admitted anchors, rather than reconstructing their existence only from marker
43	paths. Any optional observed count belongs to provenance, not source scope or
44	Run identity.
45	
46	This needs an explicit versioned successor to DiscoveryProvenanceV1 and
47	AdmittedBoundaryInventoryV1, their schema mirrors, native discovery result and
48	host integration. Do not add the fields to old closed records or silently
49	reinterpret a frozen exact-count claim. Required controls: unreadable pruned
50	directory; empty supplied descendant inventory; 4200 synthetic observed
51	markers; changing only that optional inventory changes provenance but not
52	selected units/scope; native dependency reads still require separate custody.
53	The row is specified here; schema/model integration and new frozen-subject
54	review remain outstanding. The XA-01 reference patch does not claim to fix this.
55	
56	## XA-03 — make the graph-query availability route an explicit scoped selector
57	
58	Preserve the already explicit graph-query behavior and its retained goldens:
59	known `purged`, `expired`, `corrupt` or `unavailable` availability observations at
60	`execute_graph_query` produce operational-failed / HOST.IO_FAILURE / exit 4,
61	with their exact evidence detail. They never produce empty graph success.
62	
63	Amend identity-and-evidence §5's general precondition paragraph to say that
64	explicit graph operations use query-projection-contract.v3 §7 for this
65	observation. Reserve exit 2 there for command-specific prerequisites whose
66	owners actually select request rejection, such as attempting an operation
67	whose required evidence cannot be supplied at admission. Retained manifest-only
68	queries can still report a tombstone without reopening unavailable evidence.
69	Missing promised bytes during replay remain the existing exit-4
70	EvidenceUnavailable boundary. Do not change an exit based merely on a
71	filename, exception prefix or a caller-supplied origin.
72	
73	Add the same narrow applicability selector in the query contract's owning
74	section. The proposal changes no graph result, D9 code, fault vocabulary or
75	schema. It resolves overlapping prose so independent implementers can select
76	one route. The retained positive plus four unavailable-state public calls
77	support the current behavior; actual independent review must assess the
78	proposed selector before a successor is accepted.

103	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
104	
105	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
106	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
107	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
108	
109	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
110	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
111	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
112	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
113	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
114	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
115	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
116	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
117	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
118	
119	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
120	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
121	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
122	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
123	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
124	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
125	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
126	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and

132	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses

1	# Query projection contract (evaluator3)
2	
3	This is the intended-design law for advertised `graph.neighbors|path|reach` over an admitted evaluator3 Run. It is not product implementation, not a HydraDB store, and not a rewrite of native absence, `close_run`, sealed Run, atom evaluation, execution replay, SEAL, or storage generations.
4	
5	Schema: `schemas/evaluator3/graph-query.schema.json` `$id` `urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:evaluator3:graph-query:3`, `schemaMajor` **3**. All **20** operation names are unchanged. The other **17** operations keep their existing Params bag, owners, and (for snapshot metadata) request-shaped `View` on the response. `finding.show` remains `workflow_projection_model.v3.query_finding`. Historical `workflows/schemas/graph-query.schema.json` is not this owner.
6	
7	Reference: `query_projection_model.v3.py`. The public entry `execute_graph_query` always requires a retained Run and identity-model.v3 `close_run`. Caller-authored edges, `host.standing`, `host.cache`, `host.targetAttributions`, and `host.evaluationDeficiencies` are not public graph evidence. Internal `traverse_projected_graph` may walk already-projected edges for algorithm goldens; it does not admit a Run.
8	
9	## 0. What this unit is not
10	
11	- Not a parallel absence evaluator. Zero neighbor rows is not “no callers.” Native/atom remain owners of incoming search, Coverage, and closed-world.
12	- Not a new global database id and not a FactViewId recipe. Endpoints are evaluation-subject tuples. Fact-views are existing `view2:` identities.
13	- Not a numeric backend identity or backend default order.
14	- Not an exact accelerator presented as a semantic producer (GX-01). Physical CSR/GraphBLAS/SQLite remain private if they preserve exhaustive parity with the canonical fact-view walk for the declared query.
15	- Not a change to native/input prefixes (`snapshot2`, `plan2`, `closure2`, `import2`, `fact2`, `view2`) or sealed output prefixes (`run3`, `finding3`, `evidence3`).
16	- Not a cache of projected edges. A derived cache is not completeness. GX exact fallback is the admitted fact-view walk.
17	
18	## 1. Selection: Project, Run, fact-views
19	
20	The admitted Run is authority. A derived resolver or host index is not permission to answer a different historical selection.
21	
22	| Selector | Law |
23	|---|---|
24	| `projectId` | Required. Must equal the admitted Run’s project. |
25	| Request `view` | `{runId}` or `{snapshotId}` or `{latest: true}`. |
26	| Graph effective view | Unique concrete `run3`. Response `resolvedView` is `{runId}` only. |
27	| `{runId}` | Must equal `close_run` identity. |
28	| `{snapshotId}` | Must equal `run.snapshotId` of the admitted Run **and** an explicit complete trusted host resolver observation `host.runsForSnapshot[snapshotId]`. Missing or empty observation → `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN` / `QUERY.VIEW_UNKNOWN` (one admitted Run does not prove uniqueness). More than one distinct Run in the observation → `QUERY.VIEW_AMBIGUOUS`. The unique name must be the admitted Run. A stale map that names this Run for a different snapshot is `QUERY.VIEW_UNKNOWN`. The index cannot grant a wrong historical selection. |
29	| `{latest: true}` | Explicit trusted host observation `host.latestRunId`. It is never derived from static Run bytes. Missing or unequal to the admitted Run → `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN` / `QUERY.VIEW_UNKNOWN`. Continuation never re-resolves latest. |
30	| Fact-view set | Explicit `params.factViewDigests` (each an admitted `view2` of this Run) **or** all admitted views of the Run whose scopes match `relation@minResolution`. Silent “newest provider” is forbidden. A digest not on the Run → `QUERY.FACT_VIEW_UNAVAILABLE`. Explicit admitted digests that are not views of the requested relation@rung remain the selected set; if none of the selected views match, disclose `native-evidence-unavailable`. |
31	
32	Non-graph snapshot metadata operations (`availability.show`, `run.list`, …) may keep `resolvedView` in request `View` shape. Do not force `{runId}` onto those operations.
33	
34	## 2. Vertex domain and endpoint admission
35	
36	A graph endpoint is the tuple `(universe, kind, nativeSubjectId, packageManifestPath or empty)`. No persisted evaluation-subject object is required.
37	
38	**Vertex domain** of a query is the union of:
39	
40	1. Subject-inventory rows selected by the admitted proof `evaluationInputRefs` (`domain=subject-inventory`), with universe taken from the EnumerationPlan program binding `(cellOrdinal, programOrdinal)`. Package vertices include `packageManifestPath` from the inventory row path.

154	## 7. Faults (CommandEnvelope kind=failure)
155	
156	`QueryRefusal.termination()` is a StepTermination. The public failure carrier is CommandEnvelope major 3, `kind=failure`, nonempty `errors` of registered DomainDetail, and **no** `run` field. A query does not mint a Run. Reading an old Run does not commit a new Run. `runId` appears on termination only for indeterminate completeness of an already admitted Run.
157	
158	Failure `requestId` is an already reserved host observation (`host.requestId`, `req1_` + 32 hex). It is never hashed from request bytes and this reference model does not implement CSPRNG. Missing or malformed host RequestId is a **reference-call precondition** (`ReferenceCallPrecondition`), distinct from public request refusal. Optional envelope `projectId` is included only when the request projectId is schema-admitted; malformed projectId is omitted.
159	
160	Identity **availability** (foundation `EvidenceStore` / availability record) is a trusted current host observation. `purged` / `expired` / `unavailable` / `corrupt` **refuse** access (`HOST.IO_FAILURE` / `evidence.*`). The observation cannot grant retained authority: `close_run` remains the positive admission. Omitted availability is not a grant and not a purge.
161	
162	| Condition | class | errorCode / reason | domainDetail |
163	|---|---|---|---|
164	| schemaMajor ≠ 3 | request-rejected | `REQUEST.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` | `QUERY.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` |
165	| malformed graph params / extra properties / LogicalPath endpoint | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.PARAMS_MALFORMED` |
166	| unsupported relation or non-projectable request rung | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.RELATION_UNSUPPORTED` |
167	| malformed-complete but ambiguous endpoint | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.ENDPOINT_AMBIGUOUS` |
168	| well-formed endpoint outside the vertex domain | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.ENDPOINT_UNKNOWN` |
169	| two Runs named for one snapshot | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.VIEW_AMBIGUOUS` |
170	| empty, missing, stale, or mismatched latest/snapshot/run selector | request-rejected | `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN` | `QUERY.VIEW_UNKNOWN` |
171	| cursor bind mismatch | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.CURSOR_MISMATCH` |
172	| view2 not admitted on this Run | request-rejected | `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` | `QUERY.FACT_VIEW_UNAVAILABLE` |
173	| missing retained bytes | operational-failed | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (`faultCause=host-io`) | `evidence.missing` |
174	| corrupt retained bytes | operational-failed | `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (`faultCause=host-io`) | `evidence.corrupt` |
175	| work bound under completeness=required with owed work | indeterminate | reason `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` | (reasonCodes; success/truncated body still a query result, not kind=failure) |
176	
177	## 8. Strong wrapper versus internal traversal
178	
179	`execute_graph_query(request, run, objects, blobs, host)`:
180	
181	1. Admit request (schema major 3, closed params).
182	2. Require retained `run`/`objects`/`blobs` and call `close_run`.
183	3. Join request view to the admitted Run (`runId` / `snapshotId` / trusted `latestRunId`).
184	4. Project from admitted views, retained payloads, selected subject-inventories, and retained TargetAttributionV2 records named by the Run’s `evaluationInputRefs`. Occupancy identity follows the same normative reconciliation and exact-id derivation in atom evaluation §2 and the selected TargetAttributionV2 join law. The reference helper is an implementation of those laws, not an additional normative input. Historical V1 sidecars are not selected. Ignore `host.cache`, `host.standing`, `host.targetAttributions`, and `host.evaluationDeficiencies`. Do not read ambient unselected store blobs.
185	5. Admit requested endpoints against the vertex domain.
186	6. Traverse under the single visit-budget law.
187	7. Disclose retained Coverage, deficiencies, unresolved-edge, and incoming-search records.
188	
189	`traverse_projected_graph` walks caller-supplied projected edges for algorithm goldens only.
